description.narrative: A well-functioning dairy value chain in Nigeria

The MilkyWay Partnership was a collaboration between Arla, SEGES Innovation, DAFC, CARE, MVCF, and CORET, supporting job creation and market-driven sustainable growth in Nigeria's dairy value chain. The project established a comprehensive training and capacity-building framework, increasing milk production among local farmers and enabling the production of higher-quality milk and dairy products. It also successfully improved responsible business conduct and stakeholder cooperation within the dairy value chain. Pastoralist dairy farmers increased production and household income, despite insecurity and challenges from supply chain disruptions following COVID-19. The project developed a long-term strategy to ensure a consistent supply of high-quality milk through three sources: Smallholder dairy farmers, the Damau Household Milk Farm, and the Arla Farm.
The establishment of dairy value chain forums facilitated critical dialogue and addressed key challenges, enhancing sector collaboration. The MilkyWay Partnership and the value chain approach have inspired Kaduna State, which, in turn, is promoting the development of the Damau Household Milk farm as well as the Arla Farm into a showcase for sustainable and productive sedentary milk production in Damau. A landmark decision within Arla’s Sustainability Strategy was the investment in its first farm outside Europe – the Arla Farm in Damau - demonstrating a commitment to setting global standards in dairy farming.
The Danida Market Development Partnerships programme (DMDP) is designed to support commercially oriented partnerships for sustainable market development in developing countries. In addition to reporting on individually determined outputs and outcomes, all DMDP projects report on five key programme indicators. These five indicators are the same for the whole project portfolio, enabling strategic and programme level monitoring, and aggregation of results.
